key_insight: Machine-learned or computed density of states can effectively triage Heusler alloys for thermoelectric potential, but only explicit band-structure checks reliably confirm whether a useful gap exists.
engineering_relevance: This workflow enables much faster discovery of thermoelectric candidates by reducing expensive transport calculations while still recovering many known high-performing half-Heuslers.
method: Used DOS from both DFT spectra and neural-network predictions to prioritize compounds for transport calculations.
Validated screening quality with 3,625 band-structure and transport calculations, then certified top candidates.
evidence_signal: Across 51,257 DFT-based and 54,978 ML-based screenings, the DOS-derived Seebeck indicator ranked most compounds passing transport and stability tests within the top 1%, and 10 of 11 known half-Heusler thermoelectrics were recovered.
watch_item: Spectral-similarity metrics can miss lost band gaps in predicted DOS, so screening should be paired with band-structure verification before claiming a viable thermoelectric gap.
paper_title: High-throughput screening of Heusler alloys for thermoelectrics combining machine-learned densities of states and first-principles transport
